question: Can SyncNet (LSE-C / LSE-D) separate a speaker's own audio from the same picture with its audio shifted 300-500 ms or replaced by another speaker's, on the labelled set of calibration.json (20 bearded, 14 clean-shaven segments), where the lip-opening correlation could not (E119)?
method: Same sources and segments as calibration.json (Wikimedia Commons, 480p VP9 transcodes). Measured through the production code (review of #457): lipsync_check.face_track(source, start=t0, duration=t1-t0, keep=True) decodes the segment once at 25 fps (ffmpeg fps filter, complete-decode check) and keeps each frame as a JPEG (quality 95, as syncnet_python); face box per frame = the extent of all landmarks of the pinned MediaPipe Face Landmarker (lipsync_check.MODEL_SHA256, mediapipe 0.10.35, VIDEO mode); crop and 224 x 224 resize as syncnet_python crop_video (lipsync_check.face_crops); lipsync_check.sync_measure with the audio from lipsync_check.pcm(start, duration); SyncNet syncnet_v2.model (syncnet.SYNCNET_SHA256) in numpy (syncnet.py), 16 kHz mono audio. Positives 'pos' = the segment's own audio; negatives = audio taken from t0-0.5/-0.3/+0.3/+0.5 s of the same source ('shift-500ms' etc.) and the swap_with segment's audio ('swap'). 'mdist' = the distance averaged over the clip at offsets -15..15 frames (index k is offset 15-k): offset, conf and min_dist follow from it (syncnet.measure_mean). Media are not kept.

gate.centre: the positives of the sources that are in sync read exactly -1 or -2 (28 of 28; all 34: median -2, mean -1.68): the window is centred on their middle, -1.5, with +-1.5 frames (offsets -3..0). Centred on 0 (+-2, the first version) it was lopsided: -2 at its edge, +1 and +2 empty of real speech.
gate.margin: confidence: inside -3..0 the only negative is d00c swap at 0.796 (1.90 under 2.7) and the lowest positive is 3.745 (1.05 over); offset: the nearest shifted negatives read -4 (c01 -300 ms, 1 frame outside the window) and +3 (c02 +300 ms, 3 frames outside)
gate.missed: c01a-c (offset +3) and c02a-c (offset -5): every segment of these two sources reads the same offset, about +120 ms and -200 ms from the -1..-2 of the other sources and of the Pavo calibration clip; their shifted copies move by the applied shift (a property of the source soundtrack, not of the beard: c00, c06 and c07 bearded pass 14/14)

tracking: offset(shift) - offset(pos) equals the applied shift (7.5 / 12.5 frames) within 0.5 frame in 133 of 136 shifted negatives; the 3 others are c02 at -500 ms, beyond the +-15 frame search (-5 - 12.5)
cpu: median per 8 s segment on 4 cores: 4.4 s decode + face landmarker + JPEG, 17.0 s SyncNet (196 windows)
